verdict.rationale: LightSprint's own docs say users describe a change in plain English and the product builds it. For larger features, users plan first, pick options and mockups, and then hand the plan off as one implementation task. The scoping step is a team-driven planning flow, not clearly an automatic conversion of a plain-language description into a scoped task. missing for 10: explicit documentation that a plain-language feature or bug description is automatically decomposed and scoped into a task without manual planning, detail on how task scope is determined, and independent or hands-on corroboration (all evidence is vendor-claimed).

support.subject: As a developer, I can describe a feature or bug in plain language and have it automatically turned into a scoped implementation task

citations.quote: Describe the change in plain English. LightSprint builds it, spins up a live preview, and prepares for engineering review.
For larger features, plan first and align as a team. Pick options and mockups before anything is built, then hand the plan off as one implementation task.
Create LightSprint tasks directly from Slack, Linear, or Jira. Updates sync both ways
